claim: Around 58% of Drosophila melanogaster genes produce more than one transcript.
source: Around 58% of Drosophila melanogaster genes and >95% of human genes produce more than one transcript (Pan et al., 2008; Wang et al., 2008; Brown et al., 2014), with most human genes expressing 10 or more distinct isoforms (Djebali et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Pan et al., 2008; Wang et al., 2008; Brown et al., 2014.

claim: More than 95% of human genes produce more than one transcript.
source: Around 58% of Drosophila melanogaster genes and >95% of human genes produce more than one transcript (Pan et al., 2008; Wang et al., 2008; Brown et al., 2014), with most human genes expressing 10 or more distinct isoforms (Djebali et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Pan et al., 2008; Wang et al., 2008; Brown et al., 2014.

claim: Most human genes express 10 or more distinct isoforms.
source: Around 58% of Drosophila melanogaster genes and >95% of human genes produce more than one transcript (Pan et al., 2008; Wang et al., 2008; Brown et al., 2014), with most human genes expressing 10 or more distinct isoforms (Djebali et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Djebali et al., 2012.

claim: Some human genes are predicted to express more than 100 mRNA isoforms.
source: In genes with multiple alternative transcription start and/or pre-mRNA processing sites, their combinatorial potential exponentially increases the number of possible products, with some human genes predicted to express >100 mRNA isoforms.
evidence: The claim is stated as a prediction based on combinatorial potential of alternative processing sites.

claim: In D. melanogaster, the number of isoforms observed per gene correlates with open reading frame length.
source: In D. melanogaster, the number of isoforms observed per gene correlates with open reading frame length, suggesting that isoform complexity is a function of transcript length (Brown et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Brown et al., 2014.

claim: Isoform complexity is a function of transcript length.
source: In D. melanogaster, the number of isoforms observed per gene correlates with open reading frame length, suggesting that isoform complexity is a function of transcript length (Brown et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is presented as a suggestion based on the correlation observed and cited to Brown et al., 2014.

claim: Dscam1 generates 38,016 distinct mRNAs, each encoding a unique protein isoform.
source: The current record holder in this regard is Dscam1, in which four regions of mutually exclusive cassette exons combine to generate a remarkable 38,016 distinct >7000 nt mRNAs, each encoding a unique protein isoform (Schmucker et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Schmucker et al., 2000.

claim: Dscam1 mRNAs are greater than 7000 nucleotides long.
source: The current record holder in this regard is Dscam1, in which four regions of mutually exclusive cassette exons combine to generate a remarkable 38,016 distinct >7000 nt mRNAs, each encoding a unique protein isoform (Schmucker et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Schmucker et al., 2000.

claim: In Dscam1, the four regions of mutually exclusive cassette exon splicing are separated by one to eight constitutive exons.
source: In Dscam1, the four regions of mutually exclusive cassette exon splicing are separated by one to eight constitutive exons.
evidence: The claim is stated as a factual description of Dscam1 structure.

claim: More than a quarter of human genes have multiple alternative splicing regions separated by constitutive exons.
source: This feature of multiple alternative splicing regions separated by constitutive exons is shared by more than a quarter of human genes (Fededa et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Fededa et al., 2005.

claim: In many cases, alternative splicing regions are separated by more than 500 nucleotides.
source: In many cases, these regions are separated by >500 nts, the current limit for contiguous sequence output on most deep sequencing platforms.
evidence: The claim is stated as a factual observation about the distance between alternative splicing regions.

claim: The current limit for contiguous sequence output on most deep sequencing platforms is 500 nucleotides.
source: In many cases, these regions are separated by >500 nts, the current limit for contiguous sequence output on most deep sequencing platforms.
evidence: The claim is stated as a technical limitation of sequencing platforms at the time of writing.

claim: The processivity of available reverse transcriptases limits single molecule cDNA sequencing to less than 2500 nucleotides.
source: Further, high-throughput sequencing of RNA (RNA-Seq) generally requires its reverse transcription, with the processivity of available reverse transcriptases (RTs) limiting even single molecule cDNA sequencing (e.g., Pacific Biosciences) to <2500 nt (Sharon et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Sharon et al., 2013.

claim: Existing high-throughput technologies cannot readily retain connectivity information between very distant sequences within individual mRNA molecules.
source: Thus, existing high-throughput technologies cannot readily retain connectivity information between very distant sequences within individual mRNA molecules.
evidence: The claim is presented as a logical conclusion from the limitations of sequencing and RT processivity.

claim: Full-length transcripts must be inferred by piecing together multiple short overlapping reads.
source: Instead, full-length transcripts must be inferred by piecing together multiple short overlapping reads (Garber et al., 2011; Grabherr et al., 2011; Haas et al., 2013; Boley et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Garber et al., 2011; Grabherr et al., 2011; Haas et al., 2013; Boley et al., 2014.

claim: Loss of connectivity significantly limits abilities to catalog isoform abundance for widely separated regions of alternative exon use.
source: For widely separated regions of alternative exon use, this loss of connectivity significantly limits our abilities to catalog isoform abundance and understand the mechanisms underlying alternative isoform generation.
evidence: The claim is presented as a logical consequence of the inability to maintain connectivity information.

claim: Loss of connectivity significantly limits abilities to understand the mechanisms underlying alternative isoform generation for widely separated regions of alternative exon use.
source: For widely separated regions of alternative exon use, this loss of connectivity significantly limits our abilities to catalog isoform abundance and understand the mechanisms underlying alternative isoform generation.
evidence: The claim is presented as a logical consequence of the inability to maintain connectivity information.

claim: SeqZip is a method for profiling multiple distant (>1000 nt) sites of alternative splicing within individual RNA molecules.
source: Here, we describe SeqZip, a method for profiling multiple distant (>1000 nt) sites of alternative splicing within individual RNA molecules.
evidence: The claim is the primary description of the method developed in this study.

claim: SeqZip uses sets of DNA oligonucleotides termed 'ligamers'.
source: SeqZip uses sets of DNA oligonucleotides termed 'ligamers'.
evidence: The claim describes a key component of the SeqZip method.

claim: Each ligamer is approximately 40-60 nucleotides long.
source: Each ∼40–60 nt ligamer hybridizes to the 5′ and 3′ ends of a single alternatively spliced exon or the beginning and end of a large block of constitutively included exons, looping out the sequences in between.
evidence: The claim describes the design specifications of ligamers.

claim: Ligamers hybridize to the 5′ and 3′ ends of a single alternatively spliced exon or the beginning and end of a large block of constitutively included exons, looping out the sequences in between.
source: Each ∼40–60 nt ligamer hybridizes to the 5′ and 3′ ends of a single alternatively spliced exon or the beginning and end of a large block of constitutively included exons, looping out the sequences in between.
evidence: The claim describes how ligamers function in the SeqZip method.

claim: Loops created by ligamers can be hundreds to thousands of nucleotides long.
source: These loops can be hundreds to thousands of nucleotides long.
evidence: The claim describes the scale of sequences that can be looped out by ligamers.

claim: Juxtaposed ligamers hybridized to single RNA molecules are joined by enzymatic ligation with T4 RNA ligase 2 (Rnl2).
source: Juxtaposed ligamers hybridized to single RNA molecules are then joined by enzymatic ligation with T4 RNA ligase 2 (Rnl2) (Ho and Shuman, 2002).
evidence: The claim describes the ligation step of SeqZip and cites Ho and Shuman, 2002 for the enzyme.

claim: The resultant DNA ligation products capture the intramolecular connectivity among exons of interest.
source: The resultant DNA ligation products both capture the intramolecular connectivity among exons of interest and compress the sequence space necessary to identify those exons.
evidence: The claim describes a key feature of SeqZip ligation products.

claim: The resultant DNA ligation products compress the sequence space necessary to identify exons of interest.
source: The resultant DNA ligation products both capture the intramolecular connectivity among exons of interest and compress the sequence space necessary to identify those exons.
evidence: The claim describes a key feature of SeqZip ligation products.

claim: Exon connectivity is decoded by assessing the sizes or sequences of the ligation products.
source: Exon connectivity is subsequently decoded by assessing the sizes or sequences of the ligation products.
evidence: The claim describes how SeqZip results are analyzed.

claim: SeqZip does not include a reverse transcription step.
source: Because SeqZip does not include an RT step and is therefore not subject to RT processivity and template-switching limitations, it can be used to assess intramolecular connectivity between regions separated by thousands of nucleotides.
evidence: The claim describes a key feature of the SeqZip method.

claim: SeqZip is not subject to RT processivity and template-switching limitations.
source: Because SeqZip does not include an RT step and is therefore not subject to RT processivity and template-switching limitations, it can be used to assess intramolecular connectivity between regions separated by thousands of nucleotides.
evidence: The claim is presented as a logical consequence of not using reverse transcription.

claim: SeqZip can be used to assess intramolecular connectivity between regions separated by thousands of nucleotides.
source: Because SeqZip does not include an RT step and is therefore not subject to RT processivity and template-switching limitations, it can be used to assess intramolecular connectivity between regions separated by thousands of nucleotides.
evidence: The claim describes a capability of SeqZip based on its design.

claim: Relative ligation product abundance accurately reports spliced isoform abundance in the original sample.
source: Further, relative ligation product abundance accurately reports spliced isoform abundance in the original sample.
evidence: The claim describes a quantitative property of SeqZip that is demonstrated in the study.

claim: SeqZip was used to test proposed connectivity relationships among alternatively spliced exons in mouse Fibronectin (Fn1).
source: As a proof-of-principle, we here used SeqZip to test proposed connectivity relationships among alternatively spliced exons in mouse Fibronectin (Fn1) and to define the molecular diversity of fly Dscam1.
evidence: The claim describes one of the applications of SeqZip in this study.

claim: SeqZip was used to define the molecular diversity of fly Dscam1.
source: As a proof-of-principle, we here used SeqZip to test proposed connectivity relationships among alternatively spliced exons in mouse Fibronectin (Fn1) and to define the molecular diversity of fly Dscam1.
evidence: The claim describes one of the applications of SeqZip in this study.

claim: T4 DNA ligase was the only ligase reported to join DNA fragments templated by RNA when this study was initiated.
source: Although many ligases can join DNA or RNA oligos hybridized to a DNA template (Bullard and Bowater, 2006), when we initiated this study, only T4 DNA ligase was reported to join DNA fragments templated by RNA (Nilsson et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bullard and Bowater, 2006 and Nilsson et al., 2001.

claim: T4 DNA ligase catalyzes non-templated DNA ligation.
source: While T4 DNA ligase is the basis of multiple RNA-templated DNA ligation methods (Nilsson et al., 2001; Yeakley et al., 2002; Conze et al., 2010; Li et al., 2012), it also catalyzes non-templated DNA ligation (Kuhn and Frank-Kamenetskii, 2005), which would reduce SeqZip fidelity.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Kuhn and Frank-Kamenetskii, 2005.

claim: Non-templated DNA ligation by T4 DNA ligase would reduce SeqZip fidelity.
source: While T4 DNA ligase is the basis of multiple RNA-templated DNA ligation methods (Nilsson et al., 2001; Yeakley et al., 2002; Conze et al., 2010; Li et al., 2012), it also catalyzes non-templated DNA ligation (Kuhn and Frank-Kamenetskii, 2005), which would reduce SeqZip fidelity.
evidence: The claim is presented as a logical consequence of non-templated ligation activity.

claim: Both T4 DNA ligase and T4 RNA ligase 2 (Rnl2) catalyze RNA-templated DNA-DNA ligation.
source: Although all DNA ligases tested could efficiently join multiple oligos hybridized to the DNA template (Figure 2A; Bullard and Bowater, 2006), only T4 DNA ligase and RNA ligase 2 (Rnl2) joined the DNA oligos when hybridized to the RNA template.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and cited to Bullard and Bowater, 2006.

claim: Rnl2 is more active for RNA-templated DNA ligation than T4 DNA ligase.
source: Of the two, Rnl2 was more active for RNA-templated DNA ligation (data not shown) and produced <1/7 as much non-templated product as T4 DNA ligase (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Rnl2 produces less than 1/7 as much non-templated product as T4 DNA ligase.
source: Of the two, Rnl2 was more active for RNA-templated DNA ligation (data not shown) and produced <1/7 as much non-templated product as T4 DNA ligase (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Rnl2 cannot ligate DNA oligos hybridized to a DNA template.
source: Moreover, Rnl2 could not ligate DNA oligos hybridized to the DNA template, eliminating the possibility of contaminating genomic DNA confounding SeqZip (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Rnl2's inability to ligate DNA oligos on DNA templates eliminates the possibility of contaminating genomic DNA confounding SeqZip.
source: Moreover, Rnl2 could not ligate DNA oligos hybridized to the DNA template, eliminating the possibility of contaminating genomic DNA confounding SeqZip (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is presented as a logical consequence of Rnl2's specificity for RNA templates.

claim: SplintR ligase produces more non-templated DNA-DNA ligation events than Rnl2.
source: We found, however, that SplintR ligase produces more non-templated DNA–DNA ligation events than Rnl2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Another group reported RNA-templated DNA-DNA ligation by Rnl2 while this paper was under review.
source: Also, while our paper was under review, another group reported RNA-templated DNA–DNA ligation by Rnl2 (Larman et al., 2014), further validating its use in SeqZip.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Larman et al., 2014.

claim: Rnl2 can join multiple ligamers each looping out sections of the template when they are adjacently hybridized.
source: Ligation products were only observed when ligamers bound to adjacent RNA sequences; four-way ligation products were obtained only when all ligamers were present.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data described in the text and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Four ligamers designed to loop out various lengths of a 307 nt transcript condensed 244 nt of the target RNA to a 104 nt DNA.
source: Thus, ligamers designed to loop out various lengths of a template RNA can be used to condense by more than twofold the information required to assess RNA connectivity—244 nt of the target RNA was condensed to a 104 nt DNA.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data described in the text.

claim: Ligamers can condense RNA connectivity information by more than twofold.
source: Thus, ligamers designed to loop out various lengths of a template RNA can be used to condense by more than twofold the information required to assess RNA connectivity—244 nt of the target RNA was condensed to a 104 nt DNA.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data described in the text.

claim: Subsequent ligamer designs condensed connectivity information by more than 49-fold.
source: Subsequent ligamer designs condensed connectivity information by >49-fold.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from later experiments in the study.

claim: Cis-templated SeqZip products were detected by end point PCR at every target RNA concentration tested down to 0.01 nM.
source: Consistent with this, whereas cis products were detected by end point PCR at every target RNA concentration tested down to 0.01 nM, trans products were only detected when target RNAs were ≥10 nM, (Figure 2C, lower half).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Trans-templated SeqZip products were only detected when target RNAs were at or above 10 nM.
source: Consistent with this, whereas cis products were detected by end point PCR at every target RNA concentration tested down to 0.01 nM, trans products were only detected when target RNAs were ≥10 nM, (Figure 2C, lower half).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Cis hybridization products predominated even when both target RNAs were present at 50 nM.
source: But, even when both targets were present at 50 nM, semi-quantitative radioactive PCR revealed that the cis hybridization products predominated (Figure 2C, lower left).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: General conditions for SeqZip use cellular RNA concentrations at which most individual mRNAs are present at less than 1 nM.
source: Nonetheless, to disfavor trans hybridization, the general conditions for SeqZip described below use cellular RNA concentrations (10–40 ng/ml polyA+ RNA) at which most individual mRNAs are present at <1 nM.
evidence: The claim describes the optimized conditions for SeqZip based on the trans-hybridization experiments.

claim: SeqZip product ratios paralleled input RNA ratios over a 100-fold dynamic range.
source: To test this, we mixed two target RNAs at ratios varying from 100:1 to 1:100 (a 100-fold dynamic range). Radioactive PCR revealed that their respective SeqZip product ratios paralleled these input ratios over the entire series (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Jurkat cells predominantly express CD45 isoforms containing exons 5 and 6 (R56), only exon 5 (R5), or no cassette exon (R0).
source: Jurkat cells (resembling naïve, primary T cells) predominantly express isoforms containing exons 5 and 6 (R56), only exon 5 (R5), or no cassette exon (R0).
evidence: The claim is stated as known information about CD45 isoforms in Jurkat cells.

claim: U-937 cells predominantly express the R56 CD45 isoform and one containing exons 4, 5, and 6 (R456).
source: U-937 cells (resembling activated T cells) predominantly express the R56 isoform and one containing exons 4, 5, and 6 (R456; Yeakley et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Yeakley et al., 2002.

claim: SeqZip products for CD45 ranged from 132 to 260 nt, representing approximately threefold compression of connectivity information compared to RT-PCR products.
source: Reverse transcription-PCR (RT-PCR) products ranged from 365 to 848 nt, while SeqZip products ranged from 132 to 260 nt (Figure 3B), representing a ∼threefold compression of connectivity information.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Both RT-PCR and SeqZip reported the expected CD45 isoform abundances from Jurkat and U-937 cells.
source: Using RT-PCR and SeqZip, we measured CD45 isoforms from Jurkat or U-937 poly(A)-selected RNA or a 1:1 mixture of the two. Both methods reported the expected isoform abundances (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: SeqZip accurately reported relative abundances of CD45 isoforms even though detection required different numbers of ligation events.
source: Importantly, even though SeqZip detection of R456, R56, R5, and R0 required different numbers of ligation events, all relative abundances were accurately reported, even in the mixture containing all four isoforms (Figure 3B, lower right).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: It was originally reported that EDA exclusion in mouse Fn1 promotes use of the promoter-proximal 3′ splice site ('120') in the V region.
source: The original suggestion that an upstream splicing decision can affect a downstream splicing decision came from analysis of the EDA and V regions where it was reported that EDA exclusion promotes use of the promoter-proximal 3′ splice site ('120') in the V region (Fededa et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Fededa et al., 2005.

claim: The EDA and V regions of mouse Fn1 are separated by six constitutively included exons, comprising 813 nt.
source: The EDA and V regions are separated by six constitutively included exons, comprising 813 nt; thus, RT-PCR products including the EDA and V regions range from 1 to 1.6 kbp (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is stated as a factual description of Fn1 structure.

claim: RT-PCR products including the EDA and V regions of mouse Fn1 range from 1 to 1.6 kbp.
source: The EDA and V regions are separated by six constitutively included exons, comprising 813 nt; thus, RT-PCR products including the EDA and V regions range from 1 to 1.6 kbp (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is based on the structure of Fn1 and shown in Figure 3D.

claim: SeqZip ligation products for mouse Fn1 EDA and V regions were more than fivefold smaller (139-318 nt) than RT-PCR products.
source: In comparison, our SeqZip ligation products were >fivefold smaller (139–318 nt; Figure 3D,E), and they contained no intervening region of extensive nucleotide identity.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and 3E.

claim: SeqZip ligation products for mouse Fn1 contained no intervening region of extensive nucleotide identity.
source: In comparison, our SeqZip ligation products were >fivefold smaller (139–318 nt; Figure 3D,E), and they contained no intervening region of extensive nucleotide identity.
evidence: The claim is based on the design of SeqZip ligamers.

claim: Mice with modified intronic splicing enhancers were created to favor either constitutive inclusion (+/+) or exclusion (−/−) of the Fn1 EDA exon.
source: The effects of EDA inclusion or exclusion on V region splicing were previously tested by creating mice via homologous recombination with intronic splicing enhancers modified to favor either constitutive inclusion (+/+) or exclusion (−/−) of the EDA exon (Chauhan et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Chauhan et al., 2004.

claim: EDA inclusion or exclusion was as expected in the +/+ and −/− cells, respectively, in both SeqZip and PacBio data sets.
source: In both the SeqZip and PacBio data sets, constitutive EDA inclusion or exclusion was as expected in the +/+ and −/− cells, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from SeqZip and PacBio sequencing.

claim: No EDA inclusion could be detected in the +/− cells despite confirming the presence of both alleles in gDNA.
source: Unexpectedly, however, we could not detect any EDA inclusion in the +/− cells despite confirming the presence of both alleles in gDNA (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data described in the text.

claim: Neither SeqZip nor PacBio yielded any evidence for an effect of EDA inclusion or exclusion on V region splice site choice in mouse Fn1.
source: Regardless, neither SeqZip nor PacBio yielded any evidence for an effect of EDA inclusion or exclusion on V region splice site choice.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from both SeqZip and PacBio sequencing.

claim: In no case was the observed frequency of any A + V combination statistically different from the frequency expected for independent events in mouse Fn1.
source: That is, in no case was the observed frequency of any A + V combination statistically different from the frequency expected for independent events.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: The EDA and V regions of mouse Fn1 are spliced autonomously.
source: Our results thus support the view that the EDA and V regions of mouse Fn1 are spliced autonomously (Chauhan et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and supported by citation to Chauhan et al., 2004.

claim: Alternative splicing of four blocks of mutually exclusive cassette exons in Drosophila Dscam1 can potentially produce 38,016 possible mRNA isoforms.
source: For the Drosophila Dscam1 gene, alternative splicing of four blocks of mutually exclusive cassette exons (exons 4, 6, 9, and 17) can potentially produce 38,016 possible mRNA isoforms (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is stated as a calculation based on the structure of Dscam1.

claim: Previous studies suggest that all Dscam1 isoforms can be generated.
source: Previous studies suggest that all isoforms can be generated (Neves et al., 2004; Zhan et al., 2004; Sun et al., 2013), with all 12 exon 4 variants being stochastically incorporated in individual neurons (Miura et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Neves et al., 2004; Zhan et al., 2004; Sun et al., 2013.

claim: All 12 exon 4 variants of Dscam1 are stochastically incorporated in individual neurons.
source: Previous studies suggest that all isoforms can be generated (Neves et al., 2004; Zhan et al., 2004; Sun et al., 2013), with all 12 exon 4 variants being stochastically incorporated in individual neurons (Miura et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Miura et al., 2013.

claim: Long stretches of sequence identity in the constitutive exons separating each Dscam1 cluster and sequence similarity among exon 4, 6, and 9 variants can confound RT-PCR analysis.
source: Previous high-throughput methods for examining Dscam1 exon connectivity relied on RT-PCR, a technique potentially confounded by long stretches of sequence identity in the constitutive exons separating each cluster and by sequence similarity among exon 4, 6, and 9 variants (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is presented as a known limitation of RT-PCR for Dscam1 analysis and illustrated in Figure 4B.

claim: Long regions of sequence homology promote template switching during both RT and PCR.
source: Long regions of sequence homology promote template switching during both RT and PCR (Judo et al., 1998; Houseley and Tollervey, 2010); this can generate novel isoforms not originally present in the biological sample.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Judo et al., 1998; Houseley and Tollervey, 2010.

claim: Template switching can generate novel isoforms not originally present in the biological sample.
source: Long regions of sequence homology promote template switching during both RT and PCR (Judo et al., 1998; Houseley and Tollervey, 2010); this can generate novel isoforms not originally present in the biological sample.
evidence: The claim is presented as a consequence of template switching and supported by citations.

claim: SeqZip can dramatically reduce regions of sequence identity compared to cDNA or circularized cDNA approaches.
source: SeqZip can both dramatically reduce these regions of sequence of identity (Figure 4B) and introduce new exon-specific codes (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the design of SeqZip and illustrated in Figure 4B.

claim: SeqZip can introduce new exon-specific codes.
source: SeqZip can both dramatically reduce these regions of sequence of identity (Figure 4B) and introduce new exon-specific codes (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the design of SeqZip and illustrated in Figure 4C.

claim: SeqZip compresses sequence length and increases sequence heterogeneity, thereby greatly decreasing the potential for template switching compared to cDNAs created by standard RT or circularized cDNA approaches.
source: Thus, in addition to maintaining connectivity information, SeqZip both compresses sequence length and increases sequence heterogeneity, thereby greatly decreasing the potential for template switching compared to cDNAs created by standard RT or circularized cDNA approaches.
evidence: The claim is presented as a logical consequence of SeqZip's design features.

claim: Template-switched isoforms represented 34-55% of the isoforms detected in the RT-based triple-read sequencing method for Dscam1.
source: As expected, this RT-based method detected many novel transcript isoforms containing exon combinations not present in the four input transcripts (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B). These template-switched isoforms represented 34–55% of the isoforms detected, with many being significantly more abundant than one or more of the input isoforms.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Template-switched isoforms were present in the CAMSeq control data for Dscam1.
source: In light of the high rate of template switching in our triple-read sequencing approach, we reexamined the published CAMSeq control data to assess the extent of template-switching events (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B). Indeed, template-switched isoforms were present in the CAMSeq data, with many template-switched isoforms being more abundant than the low abundance input isoforms.
evidence: The claim is supported by reanalysis of published CAMSeq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 5386-5914 additional isoforms were detected in CAMSeq data whose presence could not be explained by either the composition of the 8 input RNA isoforms or by template switching.
source: Moreover, we detected 5386–5914 additional isoforms whose presence could not be explained by either the composition of the 8 input RNA isoforms or by template switching.
evidence: The claim is supported by reanalysis of published CAMSeq data.

claim: None of the 50,475 reads obtained in SeqZip control reactions were indicative of template switching.
source: Of the 50,475 reads obtained in these control reactions, none were indicative of template switching (i.e., no ligation product contained both pool 1 and pool 2 barcodes; Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Just 17 of 111,242 reads (0.015%) from Drosophila S2 cell poly(A)-selected RNA corresponded to template-switched isoforms using SeqZip.
source: Moreover, when the same differential coding approach was applied to Drosophila S2 cell poly(A)-selected RNA, just 17 of 111,242 reads (0.015%) corresponded to template-switched isoforms (Figure 5B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The SeqZip design greatly diminishes template switching.
source: Thus, the SeqZip design greatly diminishes template switching.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on template switching rates.

claim: Cognate ligamer-exon pairs had predicted hybridization energies lower than ΔG° = −67 kcal/mol.
source: Cognate ligamer–exon pairs had predicted hybridization energies lower than ΔG° = −67 kcal/mol; the closest near-cognate pair was ≥12 kcal/mole higher.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational analysis of ligamer-exon hybridization energies.

claim: The closest near-cognate ligamer-exon pair had hybridization energy at least 12 kcal/mol higher than cognate pairs.
source: Cognate ligamer–exon pairs had predicted hybridization energies lower than ΔG° = −67 kcal/mol; the closest near-cognate pair was ≥12 kcal/mole higher.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational analysis of ligamer-exon hybridization energies.

claim: Only 642 of 50,475 high-confidence alignments (1.3%) in control experiments contained ligamers for exons not present in any input transcript.
source: In the control experiments containing just three Dscam1 isoforms, only 642 of 50,475 high-confidence alignments (1.3%) contained ligamers for exons not present in any input transcript, with the majority of these species (221/236) represented by three or fewer reads (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: SeqZip accurately reported input cognate isoform abundances over 3 orders of magnitude for Dscam1.
source: On the other hand, SeqZip accurately reported input cognate isoform abundances over 3 orders of magnitude (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: SeqZip proved highly quantitative for assessing the majority of Dscam1 isoforms.
source: Thus, as with CD45 and Fn1 isoforms, SeqZip proved highly quantitative for assessing the majority of Dscam1 isoforms.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the quantitative accuracy demonstrated for CD45, Fn1, and Dscam1.

claim: Ligamers targeting every exon variant in Dscam1 clusters 4, 6, and 9 together with ligamers for constitutive exons 3, 5, 7, 8, and 10 reduced the median size of mRNA sequences analyzed from 1734 nt to 356 nt.
source: Ligamers targeting every exon variant in clusters 4, 6, and 9 together with ligamers for constitutive exons 3, 5, 7, 8, and 10 (97 ligamers in all) reduced the median size of mRNA sequences analyzed from 1734 nt (1722–1751 nt for exons 3–10) to 356 nt for a seven-ligamer product formed by six ligation events.
evidence: The claim is supported by the design and experimental implementation of SeqZip for Dscam1.

claim: This approximately fivefold length reduction allowed Dscam1 products to be fully sequenced using 250 bp, paired-end reads in a single Illumina MiSeq run.

claim: All 97 possible exons represented in the Dscam1 ligamer set were detected except exon 6.11.

claim: S2 cells were the least diverse in Dscam1 isoform expression.

claim: 4-6 hr embryos had intermediate Dscam1 isoform diversity.
